summary_paragraph: A male patient with a complex history including type 1 diabetes, kidney transplant, gastroparesis, cirrhosis, and atrial fibrillation was admitted for nausea, vomiting, and inability to tolerate oral intake. He presented with lethargy and altered mental status, prompting a lumbar puncture which showed elevated protein but no infection, consistent with resolving toxic metabolic encephalopathy. Imaging revealed transient hydronephrosis in one transplanted kidney, which resolved with Foley catheter placement. His symptoms improved with supportive care, nausea control, and medication adjustments. He regained mental clarity, resumed oral intake, and was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up for repeat renal ultrasound and outpatient lab monitoring.
problems: Type 1 diabetes mellitus with diabetic chronic kidney disease
